answer: Stake-bonded hardware fingerprint registry. A node hashes CPU serial plus disk UUID into a root-of-trust fingerprint and posts a 750-POA bond. The registry binds that fingerprint to one identity and rejects a second identity from the same hash within 24 hours. On duplicate, the bond is slashed and the device frozen 30 days. Unbonding needs a 30-day window so a fleeing attacker cannot recycle the stake. One hundred clones cost 75,000 POA in bonds plus one real hardware fingerprint each, not a soft config change. A notary stamps each quill with a nectar seal before anchoring a name.
